chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Or those whose keys you possess or your friend,' he said: 'These are the ones Allah named in this verse; one eats from dates and bread without their permission, and likewise the woman eats without her husband's permission. As for other food besides that, then no.'
ai.seo_question: What foods can be eaten without permission according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the phrase 'those whose keys you possess' is interpreted specifically as dates and bread, establishing a legal precedent for informal consumption (akl bi-ghayr idhn) of these staple foods without explicit permission. The hadith extends this permissibility to a wife consuming from her husband's store of these items, while clarifying that other types of food remain subject to the general rule of requiring consent, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between common staples and other provisions.
